title: India, Russia Expand Talks on Building 105 Regional Aircraft Ahead of BRICS
excerpt: Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu says New Delhi and Moscow have widened talks on manufacturing the IL-114 turboprop and Sukhoi Superjet 100 in India, targeting the UDAN regional connectivity push.
body:
• Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu met Russia's Industry and Trade Minister Anton Alikhanov in New Delhi on Thursday, expanding talks on manufacturing the turboprop IL-114 and the Sukhoi Superjet 100 (SJ-100) in India.
  • The discussions centre on the MoU between Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and Russia's United Aircraft Corporation (UAC) for licensed joint production of the SJ-100, with localisation talks reportedly nearing completion.
  • Proposed deals cover 105 regional aircraft for Indian operators including Pinnacle Air, Air Kerala and Sleek Aviation, aimed at India's UDAN regional connectivity scheme.
  • UAC head Vadim Badekha has said first Indian-built Superjets could roll out within three years, with Indian and nearby markets potentially absorbing 200–300 aircraft.

Days before the BRICS Summit convenes in New Delhi, India and Russia have widened their most ambitious civil-aviation conversation yet: building Russian-designed passenger aircraft on Indian soil. Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu said on Thursday that the two sides have "expanded the dialogue" on manufacturing the turboprop IL-114 and the Sukhoi Superjet 100 in the country.

Naidu held what he called a "warm and productive meeting" with Russia's Minister of Industry and Trade, Anton Alikhanov, focused on the Memorandum of Understanding between Hindustan Aeronautics Limited and Russia for aircraft manufacturing in India.

Two aircraft, one connectivity plan

"There are two kinds of planes. One is the turboprop IL-114, and also the Sukhoi Superjet 100, which is a jet-engine plane," Naidu told reporters. "So these two are quite compatible with our regional connectivity scheme. With a lot of airports coming up, it is very important for us to connect them. And these planes are very efficient for us to connect them. So we have expanded the dialogue on that. And we want to start the process as soon as possible of getting their planes manufactured in the country."

HAL and UAC previously signed an initial agreement for the licensed joint production and support of the SJ-100 in India, with localisation talks reportedly nearing completion. In a post on X after the meeting, Naidu wrote: "With the immense potential of regional connectivity, there is a strong opportunity for India and Russia to take our relationship from buyer-seller to joint manufacturing and deeper industrial cooperation."

"With the immense potential of regional connectivity, there is a strong opportunity for India and Russia to take our relationship from buyer-seller to joint manufacturing and deeper industrial cooperation."

— Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, Civil Aviation Minister

105 aircraft and counting

Discussions and proposed deals cover potential deliveries and arrangements for 105 regional aircraft to Indian operators, including Pinnacle Air, Air Kerala and Sleek Aviation. Russia displayed its regional SJ-100, MC-21 and Il-114-300 aircraft at the Innoprom event in Delhi to target India's expanding regional connectivity needs.

The scale could grow. UAC head Vadim Badekha told Russian news agency TASS in June that Indian carriers had expressed strong demand for the SJ-100 and Il-114-300: "We are talking about 100-200 aircraft." He said production of the first Superjet in India could begin within three years, called an output of 20–40 units a year a "good pace," and estimated the potential of the Indian and nearby markets at 200–300 aircraft.

Why the SJ-100 fits India

The SJ-100 is a twin-engine, narrow-body short-haul jet seating 103 passengers with a range of 3,530 kilometres, capable of operating from -55°C to +45°C — a range that covers Indian conditions. More than 200 have been built and are operated by over 16 airlines worldwide. HAL has called the aircraft "the game changer for short-haul connectivity under the UDAN Scheme," noting that India will need more than 200 jets for regional connectivity over the next decade. "The manufacturing of the SJ-100 aircraft marks the beginning of a new chapter in the history of the Indian aviation industry," the company said.

Background: beyond defence

The growing aviation engagement comes as Russia seeks to deepen industrial cooperation with India beyond traditional defence platforms such as the MiG and Sukhoi fighter jets — and as India pursues self-reliance in civil aviation manufacturing. HAL's original MoU with Russia was signed amid US tariff pressure on Indian exports, underscoring New Delhi's interest in diversifying industrial partnerships.

What's next

With localisation talks nearing completion, the focus now shifts to firm orders, production timelines and the mechanics of licensed manufacturing. The BRICS Summit — where Naidu said India has taken "necessary steps to ensure an impactful session" — will be the backdrop for whatever comes next. Watch for whether the 105-aircraft framework converts into signed contracts before the summit closes.
